passages.note: Bill details page naming Mishler as the Senate sponsor of HB 1002 (2022); it prints the sponsorship line but not the operative statutory text.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Ryan Mishler, Sen. Travis Holdman, Sen. Lonnie Randolph.

passages.provision_quote: (b) Each taxable year, a tax at the following rate of adjusted gross income is imposed upon the adjusted gross income of every resident person, and on that part of the adjusted gross income derived from sources within Indiana of every nonresident person: (1) For taxable years beginning before January 1, 2015, three and four-tenths percent (3.4%). (2) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2014, and before January 1, 2017, three and three-tenths percent (3.3%). (3) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2016, and before January 1, 2023, three and twenty-three hundredths percent (3.23%). (4) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2025, three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%).
passages.note: Enrolled text of the instrument Mishler sponsored; the operative amendment to IC 6-3-2-1 cuts the individual adjusted gross income tax rate paid by every resident person, with further conditional step-downs to 2.9%.
Mishler voted Yea on the conference committee report, but the tally shows no votes against, so this vote cannot carry the chair on its own (V4.1).

rows.reasoning: Mishler was the Senate sponsor of HB 1002 (2022), whose operative amendment to IC 6-3-2-1 sets the rate "imposed upon the adjusted gross income of every resident person" at "three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%)" for 2023 and 2024, down from 3.23%, with conditional step-downs to 2.9%, alongside repeal of the utility receipts tax with mandated customer rate reductions. Cutting the rate every Indiana income taxpayer pays is "Cut taxes broadly, including the main rates most people pay", and the annex settles that a main-rate cut sits here however small rather than being a "targeted adjustment". It is not "Cut taxes as far as possible and shrink what government does": the bill reduces no government function, and the later reductions trigger only if general fund revenue grows and the pension account is funded. The 50-0 conference committee vote is near-unanimous and so does not carry the chair itself; the sponsorship does.
